heroHeadline: FIFA Crisis Widens: Dutch Federation Says Infantino Must Go, Demands Full Governance Overhaul
heroSubtitle: Six weeks after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time to win the World Cup Final at MetLife Stadium (July 19), the fallout for FIFA president Gianni Infantino has moved from federation defections into formal legal jeopardy — and now into a call to restructure FIFA itself. The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB), one of FIFA's seven founding members, said Aug 30 it had lost confidence in Infantino and, unlike most federations demanding only his exit, called for power to shift from the presidency to FIFA's secretary-general and proposed an international reform summit in Amsterdam ahead of the March 18, 2027 election in Rabat. It came days after Italy's football federation (FIGC) withdrew support for his re-election bid (Aug 26), and after court filings in Manhattan and southern Florida revealed UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code for 'criminal mismanagement,' seeking discovery from two Florida-based FIFA entities over the abandoned stake-sale plan's $4.2 billion valuation, which UEFA's lawyers called 'fraudulently off-market' (Aug 27). It follows a widening federation revolt through August — FIFA fired COO Kevin Lamour (Aug 17) after he accused Infantino of misleading staff; Infantino defied a CONCACAF request and attended a Caribbean Football Union event in the Dominican Republic (Aug 22); all six Nordic federations declared 'lost confidence' in him (Aug 23); and UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin said Infantino must either step down or 'have a candidate against him' at the March 2027 election (Aug 24).
